sha256_rule: sha256 of the UTF-8 bytes of the wording's `questions` object serialised with sorted keys, separators (',', ':') and ensure_ascii false. tools/jev_steps.py refuses to run if any hash differs, so editing a wording means a new name and a new hash, never an in-place change.

j1-v1.origin: E1 shadow test on the K-2036 record (run_meta.py): one order, candidates described as documents checked against the repository

p.instructions: `verdict` is one judge's blind pairwise verdict between two candidate documents, scored with the rubric in `rubric`. Is this judge's verdict (its WINNER) correct, meaning a careful evaluator who checks every factual claim against the repository would pick the same winner?

j1-v2.origin: live Arena of the Jev panel (jev_arena.py): the candidates are named in the text; asked with both candidate orders, the verdict's A/B labels swapped with them

p.instructions: `verdict` is one judge's blind pairwise verdict between `candidate_A` and `candidate_B`, scored with `rubric`. Is this judge's verdict (its WINNER) correct, meaning a careful evaluator who checks every factual claim would pick the same winner?

tie_handling: A verdict whose WINNER is TIE is never sent to Jev: it has no P, is excluded from J1, from natural-run labels and from AUC, and is never flagged. In a seeded Arena a TIE counts as a wrong verdict (neither candidate is defect-free), has no P, and its rate is reported.
